finding.observed: The first Settings-opening case timed out querying the Service Management button before expireAccess was called. Other later Settings cases passed. The captured DOM was truncated in the sidebar, so it does not establish the original loading-shell state or import completion timestamps.
finding.cause: The test used the default one-second findByRole deadline to cover the first asynchronous Settings module and dependency-graph load. A loading dialog exists before the loaded component, and DOM-query readiness is not the same contract as module completion. The earlier Matrix1 correction replaced a synchronous query with findByRole but still left this external prerequisite inside that short query deadline.

controlledReproduction.method: A task-isolated copy of the actual WEB/shared sources preserves the production loader and Settings implementation. Only an import-factory gate holds the real module. The original default DOM query fails while the valid, closable loading dialog remains; releasing the gate makes the real Service Management button available and the original access-expiry/renewal/draft/unknown-operation assertions pass.
controlledReproduction.limit: This controlled admissible ordering confirms the missing prerequisite. It does not claim to replay the exact unrecorded Hosted loader schedule or prove an additional production authorization race.

repair.behavior: After each real Settings/Terminal first-open action, explicitly await that exact module import inside React act before querying its controls. This awaits the actual module/dependency promise without eager preloading before the user action. Workspace handoff uses the same boundary even when its Settings body is mocked. The newly added regression controls the production deferPanel loader promise, dynamically imports the actual Settings graph, closes the pending panel, and verifies late completion cannot resurrect the old owner; explicit reopening uses the loaded component, preserves the draft, loads once and performs no API operation.
preserved: All original authentication-expiry, modal ownership, draft preservation and unknown-operation/no-replay assertions remain unchanged.
Terminal mount/disposal and return-to-chat assertions remain.
Default query/test timeouts, worker count and retry policy are unchanged.
Dedicated deferred-panel tests continue to cover failed imports, explicit retry, close while pending and hidden terminal preservation.
No production loader, security boundary, provider, conversation or deployment implementation was changed.

analogousConsumers.result: Updated every Settings-opening action in app-lifecycle, the cold Settings route in draft-navigation, the mocked Settings handoff route, and the first TerminalOnDemand route. Direct Settings/Terminal unit consumers are synchronously imported and do not have this deferred-module prerequisite. No production race was demonstrated, so production behavior was retained.

details: Initial new regression used a gated mocked-import registry and vi.dynamicImportSettled; the first targeted run failed because that broad utility could return before the gated importOriginal graph completed. This intermediate test was not accepted as a production finding.
A planned edit used an unavailable Windows Python execution alias; it made no changes. The next same-source invocation accidentally ran and passed. That retry is retained but is not repair evidence.

Awaiting the exact Settings import fixed the asynchronous prerequisite, while the mocked-import fixture then exposed duplicate mock-factory execution from concurrent direct imports. The final regression now gates the real loader at the production deferPanel boundary and awaits its exact promise; it does not mock the module registry or weaken the one-load assertion.
Final accepted evidence is the complete six-module run against that final fixture, not either intermediate passing/failing attempt.

whyEarlierChecksMissed: Earlier local matrices and targeted tests included the original case and were green, but they did not establish module completion separately from the query deadline or control a pending real import. Local success therefore did not prove the first-open boundary under Hosted cold loading.
prevention: For tests exercising a control inside an on-demand module, first await the exact module prerequisite after the open action, then assert DOM behavior. Keep separate controlled real-module coverage for pending, failure, explicit retry and close-before-completion; never solve this by raising DOM deadlines, suppressing failures or replacing a real feature with a placeholder.
limitations: No full suite, hosted rerun, paid model, external MCP or live service mutation was performed by this repair task.
A clean new full-repository source audit and the required final matrices/Hosted checks remain release gates.
